items.title: Elden Ring Tarnished Edition Gameplay Showcase Details Switch 2 Release
items.summary: Bandai Namco released a new Elden Ring Tarnished Edition gameplay showcase ahead of its August 28 launch on Nintendo Switch 2.
items.content:
Bandai Namco has released a new Elden Ring Tarnished Edition gameplay showcase ahead of the game’s August 28 launch on Nintendo Switch 2.

The video gives Nintendo players a closer look at character builds, spirit summons, co-op play, and the expanded package coming to the platform.

The gameplay showcase highlights how players can shape their Tarnished through combat style, gear, and player choice.

It also shows spirit summons, which can help turn difficult fights by drawing enemy attention or adding extra pressure during battles.

The trailer also points to online play, with players joining others to take on some of the game’s larger threats.

Elden Ring Tarnished Edition brings the full FromSoftware and Bandai Namco action RPG to Nintendo Switch 2, including the Lands Between and the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion.

Tarnished Edition includes the base game, Shadow of the Erdtree, and extra content made for this release.

That includes two new starting classes, new character armor, and the ability to customize Torrent, the player’s mount.

Elden Ring Tarnished Edition is available to pre-order now on Nintendo Switch 2.

The added starting classes, armor, and Torrent customization options will also be sold separately for Elden Ring on PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S, and PC via Steam.

items.title: Elden Ring Tarnished Edition Gets Another Pre-Launch Trailer
The Duskbloods outshines Elden Ring as 14 starting classes leak online
items.summary: There's definitely a build for everyone in The Duskbloods.
items.content:
You've got plenty of choices within The Duskbloods to find a build that's suitable for you.

Elden Ring is widely regarded as one of the greatest games of all-time - and certainly of this decade.

FromSoftware’s GOTY winner landed back in 2023, bringing with it a comprehensive list of 12 starting classes.

Those were Hero, Bandit, Astrologer, Warrior, Prisoner, Confessor, Wretch, Vagabond, Prophet, Samurai, Heavy Knight, and Idus Knight.

However, FromSoftware’s upcoming The Duskbloods is set to outshine its predecessor with its more comprehensive offering, as a whopping 14 starting classes for The Duskbloods have leaked online.

The Duskbloods is very much a game that’ll tread new ground for FromSoftware.

While it shares a visual kinship with Bloodborne thanks to its Victorian gothic setting, The Duskbloods is unlike anything in its developer’s back catalogue, being FromSoftware’s first PvPvE action game. It’s also notably a Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive.

As for those 14 starting classes, well, they surfaced on Famiboards ahead of a closed network test, as spotted by MyNintendoLife .

“The sole survivor of an extinct clan of rare-blood hunters. He uses his extraordinary sense of smell to track the blind spots in others’ pasts. He descended into madness after repeatedly licking the blood spatter from his sister—whom he himself had killed—and still walks the line between life and death in search of pure blood.”

“An executioner of the Marisbel Inquisition. He carries a massive iron guillotine blade on his back. Having been exposed to too much blood over the years, he has begun to mutate himself, and now wanders in search of the “Blood of the Beginning” before his own head is severed.”

“A blind nun abandoned in the basement of a ruined cathedral. She inflicts self-harm to spread the grotesque blood blisters multiplying inside her body. The footprints she leaves behind instantly cause anything they touch to rot.”

“A fanatic saint who drives silver nails into various parts of his body, using the flowing blood as a catalyst for miracles. By inflicting wounds on himself, he temporarily gains overwhelming ferocity, but his mind and body are already completely broken.”

“A man who continued to collect corpses on the streets of Temurat at dusk. A mud-like monstrosity that was once his family writhes inside the iron coffin he carries on his back; by slamming the coffin against enemies, he sucks up their blood and feeds it to the creature inside.”

“A deranged taxidermist who sews the flesh of beasts from all eras and regions directly onto his own body. During battle, he seizes enemy tissue and uses it to eerily patch and reinforce himself. Through the accumulation of tainted power, he transforms his own body into that of an ancient, rare beast.”

items.title: Elden Ring Gets Promising Gameplay Update on Switch 2 in New Video
items.summary: Nintendo and Bandai Namco show off Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition ahead of release
items.content:
on Google Preferred Source Google News Link copied to clipboard By Michael McWhertor Published Aug 18, 2026, 1:26 PM EDT News Looks like the Lands Between are going to be OK

Elden Ring movie officially sets release date and unveils cast Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time remake may be canceled, but the original now plays better than ever Tomb Raider remake gameplay changes have fans conflicted Elden Ring's Switch 2 version looks better than ever in new official gameplay Image: FromSoftware/Bandai Namco Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition Sign in to your Polygon.com account 2023's Game of the Year Elden Ring is finally making its way to Nintendo Switch 2 later this month after a substantial delay. The Tarnished Edition of FromSoftware's open-world action-RPG was originally pegged for a 2025 release, but after multiple reports of Elden Ring running poorly on Switch 2 , publisher Bandai Namco gave the port's developers more time to cook.

Fortunately, Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition looks like it's shaping up to be great, based on new official gameplay and video of the game running in handheld mode on Switch 2.

A new gameplay showcase video released Tuesday offers both a minute-long primer on what Elden Ring is and some evidence of how the game performs on Nintendo's handheld. For Elden Ring veterans, there's not a lot new here; the video doesn't reveal much more about the Tarnished Edition's new prebuilt starting classes. But for Switch 2 owners just getting their first taste of Elden Ring , it's a simple, straightforward look at what FromSoft's game has to offer, including cooperative multiplayer and a tough-as-nails Soulslike on the go.

In addition to the official, direct-feed gameplay of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition , there's also new video of off-screen gameplay, both in docked and handheld modes. Japanese outlet Denfaminico Gamer has nine minutes of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition running on Switch 2, showing what appears to be a very playable version of the game.

Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition has been a long time coming. The Switch 2 port was originally announced in April 2025 at Nintendo's big showcase for its new console. The Elden Ring port was revealed alongside a handful of similar Switch 2 rereleases, including Cyberpunk 2077 , Hogwarts Legacy , Street Fighter 6 , and Hitman World of Assassination .

Originally, Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition was slated to arrive in 2025, but after a rough showing at last summer's Gamescom event , developer FromSoftware and Bandai Namco delayed the game into 2026. More recent showings of the Elden Ring Switch 2 port were more promising, however. Now it appears that FromSoftware and Bandai Namco have managed to get the open-world fantasy role-playing game in working order on Nintendo's hybrid console-handheld.

Elden Ring is currently available on PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X. The Switch 2 version is coming on Aug. 28, with the Tarnished Edition bonus content available on other platforms as paid DLC.

The original release pulled in more than 400 Game of the Year nominations on its way to becoming one of the defining action RPGs of the last several years, and this version is the Switch 2's chance to get in on it.

items.title: Elden Ring Tarnished Edition Videos Showcase Improved Performance on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: After facing a delay from last year due to performance issues, FromSoftware has achieved a smooth 30 FPS for the upcoming port.
items.content:
FromSoftware’s decision to delay the release of Elden Ring Tarnished Edition on Nintendo Switch 2 to August 28th might have paid off for the studio. Videos are now popping up showcasing the open-world Soulslike running on Nintendo’s current-generation console, and compared to the last time we saw it running, there have been some major improvements made.

As you can check out in the two videos below (courtesy of Famitsu and Denfaminico), both handheld mode and docked mode were showcased. While the console wasn’t able to go all the way up to a steady frame rate of 60 FPS in either mode, the title was still running quite smoothly at 30 FPS. However, handheld mode still carries some caveats; some frame drops can be seen whenever the player takes on enemies with more going on, like large creatures or boss fights.

Generally, however, the moment-to-moment gameplay has seemingly benefited quite a bit from FromSoftware’s focus on refining the port. The fact that the title is still ten days away could also indicate that the studio has a day-one patch planned that will smooth out some of these issues.

Previews of Elden Ring Tarnished Edition running on the Nintendo Switch 2 had first popped up back in March during GDC 2026 . At the time, attending publications had noted that the game’s performance was already vastly improved when compared to what we had seen last year.

The Nintendo Switch 2 release was originally announced all the way back in April 2025, and while details weren’t quite revealed at the time, some reports started coming out in the following months indicating poor performance . One such report gave the impression that, despite a frame rate cap of 30 FPS, the Tarnished Edition version of the game often dipped down to 20, and sometimes even 15 FPS. Comparisons were made to the frame rate of Nintendo 64 title The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , which is known for running at 20 FPS.

Elden Ring was originally announced back in 2022 across PC, PS4, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S. The title is the second-latest single-player outing by the studio, and saw immensely positive critical reception . It even went on to become many publications’ game of the year at the time. In 2024, FromSoftware released the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion , which further expanded on the title’s story by giving us a glimpse at its past and two of its major characters.

The core story of Elden Ring is told quite loosely, largely through strange conversations, item descriptions, and environmental storytelling. It puts players in the shoes of the Tarnished One who has been Marked by Grace, and has been tasked by a strange woman with acquiring the Great Runes to reforge the eponymous Elden Ring.

Throughout your time with the game, you slowly learn about the machinations of the Greater Will, the various factions all vying for power over the Empty Throne, the ultimate fate of the previous rulers of the land, and the reason why everyone seems to be stuck in a never-ending war.

Platforms: PS5, Xbox Series X, PS4, Xbox One, PC

items.title: FromSoftware significantly improved the Switch 2 version of Elden Ring before release
items.summary: The Duskbloods will get proper optimization, it seems.
items.content:
1 Источник: Elden Ring 18 August 2026, 14:35 run.code The Duskbloods will get proper optimization, it seems.

FromSoftware has significantly improved the Nintendo Switch 2 version of Elden Ring compared to last year's build. The game was originally planned for release on Nintendo's new console last year, but the developers decided to postpone the release to avoid compromising the quality of the port. Now, Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition is set to be released on August 28.

New gameplay footage was published by Japanese publications Famitsu and Denfaminico Gamer. The videos demonstrate the game's performance in both docked and handheld modes. Judging by the presented materials, the project runs significantly more stable in docked mode than in last year's version.

The game doesn't reach 60 frames per second, but in most of the shown scenes, it maintains around 30 fps. Moreover, in docked mode, there are almost no noticeable stutters even during large-scale boss battles.

In handheld mode, the situation is somewhat more complex. Overall, the game also demonstrates acceptable performance, but during boss battles, individual frame rate drops can be observed. There are still about ten days left until release, so developers can potentially further optimize the game with a final patch.

items.title: Mortal Shell 2 Review – A Bigger, Better Sequel, Clearly Inspired by Elden Ring
items.summary: Cold Symmetry delivers a confident sequel in Mortal Shell 2 with rewarding exploration, engaging combat and focused progression, despite some rough edges.
items.content:
I t’s fascinating to look at just how much FromSoftware has shaped the Soulslike genre over the years. Its influence can be felt not only in games like Lies of P and Nioh , but also in how action RPGs approach character progression, combat, level design, and even difficulty. That evolution arguably reached its peak with Elden Ring , a game that took the familiar Souls formula, expanded its sense of scale and exploration, and demonstrated just how effectively it could work within an open world.

So, why am I talking about Elden Ring in a review of Mortal Shell 2 ? Because after spending the last week with Cold Symmetry’s sequel, those inspirations are difficult to ignore, particularly in the way it approaches its world and progression, albeit in a more focused and compact fashion. More importantly, though, Mortal Shell 2 doesn’t simply live in the shadow of those influences but manages to provide its own spin specifically with regards to build and progression mechanics.

" Mortal Shell 2 doesn’t simply live in the shadow of those influences but manages to provide its own spin specifically with regards to build and progression mechanics."

The most obvious inspiration Mortal Shell 2 takes from Elden Ring is its open-world approach to level design and exploration. It isn’t as big as the Lands Between, obviously, instead focusing more on being compact and dense. On the surface, it may look like just another open world, but the deeper I ventured into it, the more familiar that design philosophy started to feel. Compared to the semi-open, hub-based structure of the first game, Mortal Shell 2 now features a far more seamless and interconnected landscape, with massive landmasses that encourage you to freely explore and carve out your own path.

There are several dungeons and beacon sites scattered across the world, with many asking you to cleanse the area or track down hidden items along the way. The overworld itself is exceptionally well designed, encouraging exploration both horizontally and vertically, while rewarding you for going off the beaten path. Although some of the dungeons and beacon-related areas can feel repetitive in structure, they still manage to look and feel distinct enough, with their own assortment of items and secrets to uncover, just like in Elden Ring . All of this is backed by fantastic art direction that constantly evokes darkness, despair and eeriness, you know, the familiar trademarks of a Soulslike game.

Individual character progression remains relatively simple: you collect Gloom, essentially the game’s equivalent of souls, and use it to raise your character level. Where progression becomes more interesting, however, is in how Mortal Shell 2 ties the discovery of new weapons, Shells, and other useful items directly into open-world exploration. The game clearly wants you to actively venture out into its world, and thankfully, it gives you enough guidance to keep that exploration focused. Want weapons like the Scythe, Crossbow or Martyr’s Blade? Simply purchase their respective maps from Merrick, the merchant, and the game will highlight a general search area rather than revealing the exact location. Looking for additional Shells works in a similar fashion, with their locations becoming available through Glimpses.

"The game clearly wants you to actively venture out into its world, and thankfully, it gives you enough guidance to keep that exploration focused. "

What I like about this system is that the resources required to uncover these locations, whether Gold Coins, Glimpses or Gloom, are fairly straightforward to obtain. As a result, exploration rarely feels aimless, with my travels constantly guided by clear objectives while still leaving enough room for discovery along the way.

However, the world of Mortal Shell 2 is intriguing enough that it’s incredibly easy to get sidetracked. Since I love exploring open-world games, I unlocked all the available map locations for items and weapons, they’re fairly cheap to procure, by the way, but even with those objectives marked out, the world itself would often pull me in a completely different direction. More than once, that curiosity led me straight into locations where an intimidating boss was roaming around, catching me completely off guard. There are a dime a dozen open-world games this generation, but Mortal Shell 2 creates that urge to explore by simplifying the systems surrounding exploration rather than constantly overwhelming you with them.

Mortal Shell 2 features eight Shells, more than double what was available in the original game, and each one brings its own abilities and playstyle to the table. For those unfamiliar with the system, Shells are essentially fallen warriors that you inhabit, with each granting access to abilities specific to that character. One, for example, can turn invisible for a set period of time, while another can perform a melee attack using a mechanical hook grafted onto their arm. Some Shells are even tied to bosses that you first need to defeat, allowing you to eventually make use of attacks you previously witnessed being used against you.

Unlocking each Shell also opens up more of its individual lore, returning from the original game in the form of short playable snippets that flesh out their respective backstories. You can access more of these by increasing your bond with a Shell, which also improves its revival efficiency. In practical terms, if you’re knocked out during combat, a stronger bond means fewer melee attacks are required before you can regain access to that Shell.

Each Shell can also be upgraded further to strengthen its defining abilities. The one I primarily used specialized in invisibility, for example, and investing in that ability allowed me to remain hidden for longer periods. Other upgrades can affect aspects such as movement speed, dodging and other traits tied specifically to the Shell you choose. Altogether, it creates an engaging progression system with plenty of room for build variety, and having that many meaningful choices available to the player is rarely a bad thing.

"The general enemy roster is also fairly extensive and changes noticeably from region to region."

Mortal Shell 2 doesn’t feature an especially large assortment of weaponry, with eight main weapons alongside a similar number of sidearms. While that may come across as a negative to some players, I think it fits the more focused experience the game is aiming for, something I touched on earlier. For most of my playthrough, I stuck with The Iconoclast, a two-handed greatsword found fairly early in the game, and simply focused on upgrading it. Although I did acquire several other weapons along the way, I found it more than capable of tearing through most of the challenges the world threw at me.

items.title: Rise with ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition, launching 28th August on Nintendo Switch 2
items.content:
The Lands Between—a place of myth, gods, and broken dreams. Long ago, Queen Marika and her divine offspring reigned here, but since the Elden Ring was shattered, the world has fallen into decay. Now, the land whispers for a King.

The ‘Tarnished’, long exiled, are finally seeing the light of Grace once more. Step into this hauntingly beautiful realm, unravel its ancient mysteries, and rise as the one true Elden Lord.

The ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition game arrives on the Nintendo Switch™ 2 system on 28th August .

The Lands Between are part of a vast continent, where magnificent open fields and huge dungeons with complex three-dimensional designs are seamlessly connected. As you explore, the joy of discovering unknown and overwhelming threats awaits you.

Mastery of the terrain and knowledge of its secrets can help you overcome enemies and defeat formidable bosses—or lead invading players into traps.

An epic drama born from a myth created by George R.R. Martin The founding mythology of Elden Ring was written by George R. R. Martin and adapted into a rich multilayered story. Intersecting goals and desires between the characters create an intense narrative that weaves throughout the Lands Between. The events of the game can unravel in many ways—depending on your interventions.

Combat is simple to learn yet offers hidden depths of dexterity. As you seek to become the Elden Lord, you’ll need to explore the balance between attacking, avoiding damage, using a wide variety of weapons, spells, summons, and perfecting your timing to take advantage of your opponents’ weaknesses.

Create and build your own character In addition to customising the appearance of your character, there are countless ways to combine the weapons, armour, usable items, and magic that you equip. You can develop your character according to your play style.

No matter if you prefer bold physical confrontation, tactical spellcasting, or the subtle art of stealth, you’ll be able to find gear that supports your choices.

Traverse together with other Nintendo Switch 2 players. You can play with up to two other Tarnished as your cooperative teammates, either by inviting them using a shared password or by summoning them from a pool of nearby community members.

There are also ample opportunities to face off against other players, either through co-op invasions, invited duels, or the many player battle options available in the three Colosseums.

If you’d like to learn more or begin your journey to the Lands Between by pre-ordering the Tarnished Edition, please check out the link below.

items.title: Every Soulsborne Game, Ranked From Worst to Best
items.content:
elden ring Image via FromSoftware By Robert Lee III Published Aug 13, 2026, 6:36 AM EDT Writing from the Chicagoland area in Illinois, Robert is an avid movie watcher and will take just about any excuse to find time to go to his local movie theaters. Robert graduated from Bradley University with degrees in Journalism and Game Design with a minor in Film Studies. Robert tries his best to keep up with all the latest movie releases, from those released in theaters to those released on streaming. While he doesn't always keep up with the latest TV shows, he makes it a goal to watch nearly every major new release possible. He has been honing his craft and following any and all movie news all his life, leading up to now, where he has a vast knowledge of film and film history. He also logs every movie that he watches on his Letterboxd page, and has hosted a weekly online movie night with his closest friends for over 6 years. Sign in to your Collider account Add Us Add on Google Preferred Source Google News Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap In a medium as old as video games are now, most of the time you can say you’ve seen it all. However, when Demon’s Souls was originally released back in 2009, it unleashed upon the world a new type of game that, to this day, remains one of the most influential of the past decade. Beyond the memes of “git gud," the core gameplay, environmental design, and storytelling techniques behind the Soulsborne games keep fans coming back time and time again.

With FromSoftware continuing to expand its catalog beyond the traditional Souls formula, it seems like a good time to revisit and rank the games in the Soulsborne series, while also taking a look at the closely connected titles such as Bloodborne and Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice . The games are ranked based on the strength of their combat, world and level design, bosses, atmosphere, innovation, and overall influence on the Soulsborne formula.

A still from Dark Souls 2 Image via Bandai Namco Games This shouldn’t come as that big of a surprise to anyone who’s played through all of the Soulsborne series. Though it has its fair share of fans, Dark Souls II is still far and away the worst game in the series . While the game would tighten up some areas that it was otherwise lacking in the original release with the remaster Scholar of the First Sin , the end result is still a slog to get through at times.

But with all the negatives that do surround the game, the worst Soulsborne game is still much better than a lot of other titles in the genre. There are a number of truly memorable environments included, as well as some great music (the Majula theme is arguably the best hub theme in the entire series). However, you can really tell that with series creator Hidetaka Miyazaki working primarily on Bloodborne , Dark Souls II was definitely missing something.

Image via Sony Computer Entertainment Unlike the games that will follow on this list, the quality gap between Dark Souls II and Demon’s Souls is a rather large one. When playing Demon’s Souls , it’s clear from the outset that this is the first attempt at something that will no doubt be refined as it continues. Because of that, there are a lot of small speed bumps that might leave you scratching your head if you’re playing it for the first time after already playing other entries in the series. There’s a great case to be made that, with the Bluepoint Games remake available on the PS5, it’s actually a perfect place to jump into the series for newcomers. You’ll often hear Souls veterans state that the first game you play in the series will be the one that you’ll think is the hardest, but even by that standard, Demon’s Souls is still one of the easier games in the franchise .

You’ll see certain gameplay mechanics present, like consumable healing items that don’t refill, that were partially implemented into Dark Souls II but would primarily make their return in Bloodborne . Because of that, you might be finding yourself farming some grass to make things easier on yourself. One of the biggest draws of these games is also the boss fights , and much like other aspects, you can see the idea present here in its infancy, fully realized in later games. There are your typical FromSoftware boss battles, such as the brute Flamelurker, and also traces of more abstract boss designs, like the Dragon God. There's also the expertly presented Maiden Astraea fight, which remains one of the most effective thematically presented boss battles in the entire Souls series. Though it's not near the #1 spot on this list, Demon's Souls is still worth playing, and a great blueprint of what the series would later become.

A still from Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice Image via Activision Picking up with the fast combat nature that Bloodborne succeeded with, Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice was an interesting departure from the typical Souls -like format. Though the unorthodox approach to storytelling in FromSoftware’s games is one of its most intriguing aspects, Sekiro decided to look at it from a more familiar narrative-driven angle . The end result is more welcoming to those that might have otherwise been put off by the often cryptic nature of their previous titles, which would often leave players sorting through lore in the game's menus as part of item descriptions.

A lot of the problems that people have with Sekiro stem from its more restricted nature. Though Sekiro himself has various tools that he can utilize in and out of combat, you’re restricted to one weapon. For many people, much of the fun of the Soulsborne games is the experimentation with the various weapon types, and in Sekiro that’s completely absent. With that being said, this is some of the finest combat in any FromSoftware title. When Nioh was released two years before, it left some people yearning for that type of refined, quick-paced style of combat, and Sekiro delivers heavily on that front. The fast-paced, oftentimes multiple-phased boss battles are thrilling to take part in. It's a game that rewards patience as well as aggressiveness, as mechanics like parrying act as your key to survival.

A tarnished kneeling on the ground while holding a sword in their hand in art for 'Elden Ring Nightreign' (2025) Image via FromSoftware Elden Ring Nightreign is easily the most unique entry in the franchise, acting as a complementary experience as opposed to a true continuation of the previous release. This Elden Ring spinoff instead implements a roguelike style of gameplay, with an emphasis on repeating a cycle of runs and using gained knowledge to make it farther on each attempt. This is further complemented by Nightreign being the only Soulsborne game that is envisioned as a co-op experience, built and designed for a group of three players to traverse Limveld and prepare themselves for Heolstor, the Nightlord.

Because of the inherent facets of the roguelike genre and the implementation of multiplayer, Nightreign finds itself to be arguably the most infinitely replayable experience in the entire Soulsborne franchise . It seamlessly acts as an entertaining and fulfilling companion piece to the world and overall experience of Elden Ring , creating something incredibly fulfilling without taking away any of the strengths of the original game. There will always be an inherent fun in playing through the game with friends and fighting against giant, difficult bosses together, as sharing the glory of Soulsborne gameplay in co-op is a must for any fans of the series.

Your answers point to the world your instincts were built for. This is the universe your temperament, your survival instincts, and your particular brand of stubbornness were made for.

You took the red pill a long time ago — probably before anyone offered it to you. You're a systems thinker who can't help but notice the seams in things.

The wasteland doesn't reward the clever or the well-connected — it rewards those who are hard to kill and harder to break. That's you.

You'd survive here because you know how to exist in moral grey areas without losing yourself completely.

items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stoneveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: ELDEN RING: SHADOW OF THE ERDTREE – Official Vinyl Soundtrack

items.content:
Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree.

Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set is crafted for collectors, audiophiles, and Tarnished who seek to experience the Realm of Shadow through its music.

The Collection

Housed in a full color gatefold sleeve and marked with the symbol of Messmer the Impaler, each vinyl disc is pressed on heavyweight material to ensure optimal durability and warmth of playback. Whether displayed proudly on a shelf or played to relive your own quest, this set is designed as both a collector’s piece and a lasting tribute to one of the most celebrated expansions in modern gaming.

The Artists

Across 18 tracks, the soundtrack transforms the ELDEN RING experience into a powerful standalone odyssey—one carried by orchestral grandeur, ethereal choir work, and the signature melancholy that defines the worlds created by FromSoftware.

A Collector’s Treasure

This official vinyl set is an essential centerpiece for any discerning fan’s collection. Perfect for longtime followers of FromSoftware’s musical legacy or newcomers drawn into the Land of Shadow for the first time. *This vinyl is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, Middle East, India and the United States

items.title: Discover the ELDEN RING Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp
items.summary: Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING ’s most iconic character. Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique n
items.content:
Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING’s most iconic character.

Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique night lamp captures the tragic loyalty and silent strength of Blaidd, Shadow of Ranni.

The lamp features an LED-illuminated base that reveals glowing rune symbols beneath Blaidd’s feet, evoking the grace-given power that guides Tarnished across the Lands Between. Rising above it, an engraved acrylic summoning panel glows softly when lit, capturing the look and feel of an in-game summon sign and the spirit-calling magic it represents. Powered through a simple USB connection, it offers effortless illumination for any desk, gaming setup, or collector’s display.

"If ever thou shouldst call upon me… I shall come."

Blaidd’s oath echoes still. Now, he stands ready, not for battle, but as a silent guardian of your space.

Bring the moonlit magic of ELDEN RING into your world, one glowing rune at a time.

*This edition is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia and the United States.
